newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo state initiates railway selloff - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo state initiates railway selloff - paper.

text.p: Sao Paulo state Governor Mario Covas has signed a decree for the privatization of state-owned Paulista Railway (Fepasa) and all of its assets, Estado do Sao Paulo reported.
"The objective ... is to put the entire railway and all its assets" on the auction block, the newspaper quoted the decree as saying.
The decree, which was to appear in the state's official gazette soon, calls for Fepasa to be sold at an auction. The newspaper said a minimum price for the railway would be set by state officials.

Some of the money earned from the sale would most likely go toward paying off Sao Paulo's debt to the federal government, the paper said. The state and the central government reached a landmark deal recently to restructure some $40 billion of the state's debt.
The deal required that Sao Paulo selloff many of its assets, such as railways, airports and power companies, in exchange for more lenient terms on its debt.
